key_insight: Brain-Adapter uses a dual-stream MIL design to transfer 2D biomedical vision-language knowledge to 3D brain CT diagnosis without dense voxel-level annotations.
clinical_relevance: It could enable faster, scalable multi-label screening of acute intracranial pathologies from routine CT scans, supporting critical care workflows.
method: Text-conditioned attention aligns scan features with diagnostic sentences as semantic queries.
A parallel visual MIL stream learns global scan-level signals using structured labels extracted by an LLM.
A consistency loss and uncertainty-aware refinement fuse both streams to improve ambiguous predictions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing Brain-Adapter outperforms state-of-the-art 3D models and standard MIL baselines on scan-level multi-label classification.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of report text, label extraction, and external validation across scanners, hospitals, and pathology distributions.
paper_title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies
